dailyBrief.text: Overnight: the White House waived Russia energy sanctions in a surprise move, and Pope Leo XIV is back on duty after lung tumor surgery. Markets open the week rattled — a tech selloff tied to AI spending jitters — while SpaceX's Cargo Dragon is on its way to the space station. Closer to home, rain and cold postponed Game 4 of the ALCS in Cleveland, so the Guardians wait; the Browns host Baltimore at 1 PM today. Solon woke up to frost, but it's a sunny, dry day ahead — good football weather.

weekBrief.text: Fall is in full swing in Solon: after this morning's frost, a sunny, dry stretch with highs in the mid-60s — a good week to get outside before the cold sticks around. The Browns host Baltimore today, the Cavs open at home Saturday night, and the Guardians' playoff run is on a weather pause. Grocery play of the week: Giant Eagle's free-turkey deal (spend $350 by Nov 8) stacks nicely with Meijer's $1.99/lb pork shoulder for easy dinners. Around town: pumpkin voting at the library, trunk-or-treat Thursday in Solon, and Heinen's clam bake Friday in Chagrin Falls. And the baby countdown is officially on — the checklist is loaded and ready to start checking off.

Ukraine launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia, St. Petersburg oil sites ablaze
items.summary:
Ukrainian strikes set the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchi oil depot ablaze in St. Petersburg on Sunday, in what Russia said was an attack involving more than 1,000 drones across 15 regions, Crimea and the Black Sea. One person was killed and five were wounded in St. Petersburg, and an Ozon logistics center and a VK data center were also hit, the companies confirmed.

The barrage is one of Kyiv's largest of the war and lands right in the middle of a fight with Washington: President Trump has criticized Ukraine's refinery strikes and just waived new Russia sanctions, while President Zelenskiy says Russia hit Ukrainian energy sites 76 times since the energy ceasefire was announced. Watch whether the scale of this attack hardens the sanctions debate in Congress this week.

items.title: France cleans up after its worst unrest in years, Macron to address the nation
items.summary:
France woke up Sunday to smashed shop windows, burnt-out bicycles and a partially destroyed 143-year-old town hall in Limoges after cost-of-living protests turned violent across the country. More than half a million people marched; one demonstrator died after a cardiac arrest in Paris, more than 500 officers were injured and nearly 1,800 people were arrested, including a record 855 in Paris alone.

President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence and is expected to address the nation as the clean-up runs from Lille to Marseille. The unrest merged a month-long student movement with broader anger over prices and public services, and it is now spreading — Italy saw a second day of clashes on Sunday — so European leaders face a shared cost-of-living crisis, not just a French one.

items.title: Milan police clash with protesters for a second day as Italy unrest spreads
items.summary:
Milan police fired tear gas and used water cannons on Sunday after several hundred hooded protesters broke shop windows, looted stores and set bins on fire near Piazza Duomo during cost-of-living demonstrations. More than 60 people were taken in for checks on Sunday, after 28 arrests on Saturday across Milan, Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, facing an election next year, condemned the violence and called a government meeting for Monday. Coming a day after France's riots, the Italian clashes show the protest wave jumping borders — and they put pressure on Meloni to offer a cost-of-living response without looking soft on disorder.

items.title: Fire at Alberta military base kills 4 service members, injures dozens
items.summary:
Prime Minister Mark Carney said Sunday that four Canadian service members were killed and dozens seriously injured in a fast-moving fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta on Saturday. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said 39 people were in hospital, at least 19 in critical condition, after fierce winds whipped flames beyond the base during a training exercise; officials said there is no indication of terrorism and the cause is under investigation.

Carney called it one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on home soil and ordered flags at half-staff on federal buildings. The injured — including reservists and soldiers from Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry who had gathered from across the country — overwhelmed hospitals from Wainwright to Edmonton, Red Deer and Calgary, and investigators will now focus on how a training-area fire escalated so quickly.

items.title: Pope Leo greets crowds in first public event since lung cancer surgery
items.summary:
Pope Leo XIV appeared at a window of the Vatican's apostolic palace on Sunday and spoke to pilgrims in St. Peter's Square in a firm, clear voice — his first public event since surgery five days ago to remove the lower lobe of his right lung for adenocarcinoma. He came to the window unaided, kept his usual noon appointment, and urged the crowd to set aside selfish ambitions and serve God 'without compromise.'

The appearance steadies a 17-month papacy that had been thrown into uncertainty by the diagnosis. The Vatican says Leo will ease back gradually rather than resume a full schedule at once, so his pace over the next few weeks — and any further medical updates — will signal how much the illness reshapes his agenda.

items.title: Kolkata festival stampede toll holds at 19, organizers arrested in probe
items.summary:
At least 19 people, including a 7-year-old girl, died and 25 were hospitalized Saturday night when a sudden downpour at the Chorbagan Durga Puja festival in Kolkata sent crowds rushing for cover and an announcement triggered pushing and a crush at the pavilion. By Sunday, police had arrested seven people, including organizers and security staff, and detained others for questioning.

A court-run Special Investigation Team is examining crowd control, exits and announcements at one of about 3,500 Durga Puja pavilions across the city, several of which closed temporarily as a precaution. West Bengal announced compensation and a government job for each bereaved family, on top of federal payments — but the central question for the rest of the festival is whether safety rules change fast enough to prevent a repeat.

items.title: Rubio says Trump will take up to 60 days to weigh the Russia sanctions he waived
items.summary:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Trump will take up to 60 days to assess the Russia sanctions and tariffs he waived on Friday under the Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which were due to take effect this weekend. Rubio defended a related diesel deal by arguing Russia would sell the fuel either way, and said colliding wars in Ukraine and the Middle East are driving energy prices higher at the same time.

The waiver has drawn bipartisan backlash — Sen. Thom Tillis called it 'beyond irresponsible' and Sen. Ted Cruz called it a mistake — while Zelenskiy warned it will embolden Putin, especially after Sunday's massive Ukrainian drone attack on Russian oil sites. The 60-day clock now runs into the midterms, so watch whether Congress tries to force the sanctions back on or lets the review play out.

items.title: Trump gives Netanyahu his 'complete and total' endorsement nine days before Israel votes
items.summary:
President Trump endorsed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, calling him 'Strong, Brave, and Brilliant' and a 'Great Warrior Prime Minister' in a Truth Social post addressed to the people of Israel. Trump told Axios he 'was always going to do that' and just did not want to do it too soon; Netanyahu thanked him for the 'tremendous support.' Israel votes on October 27, its first election since the October 7, 2023 attack.

Netanyahu's Likud trails centrist challenger Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar in several polls, and no candidate has a clear path to a coalition majority, so the endorsement may matter less than coalition math. Trump also warned Iran to 'change their ways, rapidly' or 'we will soon finish the job' — a reminder that the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, now in its seventh month, hangs over the vote.

items.title: Omar's lawyers demand the Justice Department return property seized from her home
items.summary:
Attorneys for Rep. Ilhan Omar asked the Justice Department on Friday to immediately return property seized in a federal search of her Washington home this week, calling the immigration-fraud investigation 'neither justified nor lawful' and a 'vindictive, retributive, and politically motivated' effort against a chief Trump critic. They say there is no legitimate basis to question her citizenship, which she obtained by naturalization in 2000.

The Justice Department called the letter 'riddled with false allegations' and said agents complied with all court orders; a magistrate judge signed the warrant but limited how the department could access her documents. The search broke the department's usual practice of avoiding public investigative steps against a candidate within 60 days of an election — Omar is on the ballot in November — so the legal fight over the warrant's limits is the next thing to watch.

items.title: Axios: Some MAGA allies discussed martial law if midterms are deemed 'rigged'
items.summary:
Axios reported that MAGA election activists on a September 30 video call pushed extraordinary measures — including martial law — if they come to believe the midterm elections are 'rigged,' with attorney Peter Ticktin, described as a Trump childhood friend, saying there 'would have to be martial law' after another rigged election. Axios noted the proposals go far beyond Trump's legal authority and that there is no evidence the elections will be rigged.

The report matters because people in that orbit have close access to the president, and it drew immediate reaction — California Gov. Gavin Newsom urged voters not to sit out the election. With 16 days to Election Day, election officials and courts, not activists, run the count, so watch for whether mainstream Republican leaders distance themselves from the talk or let it ride.

items.title: Anti-party, anti-politician candidates surge as midterms enter the final stretch
items.summary:
In red and blue states alike, unconventional candidates are downplaying or even disowning their party labels to tap voter disdain for Washington, Axios reports. The candidates come from pulpits, the NFL sidelines and outside politics entirely, but they are making the same bet: that voters are tired of career politicians.

They will not all win, but the sheer number connecting with voters is a signal about the electorate with just over two weeks left: angry and willing to take risks. If several break through on November 3, both parties will have to rethink how much a party brand helps — or hurts — in 2028.

items.title: Trump's October barrage tests his lowest approval ratings yet
items.summary:
Axios reports President Trump has packed the first half of October with controversies and breaks from convention: the federal search of Rep. Omar's home, a statement that leakers 'should be shot,' concessions to Russia, a $5,000 payment promise if Republicans hold Congress, and a Justice Department antitrust probe of major TV networks. The White House rejected the framing, saying October is 'shaping up to be another incredible month.'

A Fox News poll this week put Trump's approval at 36%, the lowest of either of his presidencies, with just 22% approving on inflation. That is the backdrop for everything else in this edition — the sanctions waiver, the early-voting push and the midterm map — and it explains why both parties are treating the next 16 days as a turnout fight above all.

items.title: AI selloff spreads to Asia as hot 3.7% inflation resets rate expectations
items.summary:
Asian markets slid after September U.S. inflation came in at 3.7% year over year, up from 3.4% and above the 3.6% expected, pushing up bets on another Fed rate hike. The damage centered on the AI trade: on Wall Street the Nasdaq fell about 1.9% and the S&P 500 about 1.1% in the initial session, with CoreWeave down roughly 16%, Dell about 11% and Oracle about 9%.

The worry is the cost of money for the AI build-out: debt-funded data-center firms borrow heavily, and higher-for-longer rates make that math harder just as revenue questions grow. The Fed meets October 27–28, and earnings from Tesla, Netflix, Texas Instruments and IBM next week will test whether real results can calm a market that CNN's Fear & Greed Index put at 18 — extreme fear — on Friday.

items.title: SpaceX earnings Tuesday will test whether AI growth justifies $18.4 billion in spending
items.summary:
SpaceX reports third-quarter results after the close on Tuesday, October 20, with Wall Street expecting revenue of about $12.89 billion, up sharply from $7.81 billion in the second quarter, and earnings of $0.14 a share versus a loss last quarter. The stock closed Friday at $146.03, down 1.74% on the day and about 10.6% over the past week, even as analysts' average price target sits near $217.50.

In the second quarter SpaceX spent $18.4 billion on capital expenditures, including $15.8 billion on AI infrastructure, while posting a $541 million net loss — exactly the spending pattern investors are punishing across the AI sector right now. Tuesday's numbers on AI revenue versus that burn rate will likely move the whole space-stock group, not just SpaceX.

items.title: Meta and Apple team up on a huge open AI model you can run on two Mac Studios
items.summary:
Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight model it calls the most capable U.S. open-weight model to date, optimized with Apple's help to run locally across two M5 Ultra Mac Studios with a combined terabyte of unified memory. The mixture-of-experts design uses about 42 billion active parameters per token, handles text, images, audio and video, and is aimed at coding and multi-step agent work; the weights are free on Hugging Face.

The partnership is the story as much as the model: Apple and Meta spent a decade fighting over ad tracking and privacy, and now Apple gets a privacy-friendly 'AI on your desk' showcase for its most expensive Mac while Meta gets distribution outside the cloud. The catch is price — a multi-Mac Studio setup runs into the tens of thousands of dollars — so watch whether labs and companies actually adopt local frontier models or stick with cloud APIs.

items.title: SpaceX Dragon delivers brain organoids and artificial-retina tech to the space station
items.summary:
SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft docked with the International Space Station on October 15 carrying more than 6,300 pounds of supplies on the company's 35th commercial resupply mission, including miniature brain organoids, 3D heart tissue and technology for producing artificial retinas in microgravity. The cargo also includes the final set of upgraded roll-out solar arrays for the station.

Researchers will use the brain and heart tissues to study diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's and to test drugs in ways that are hard to replicate on Earth, while the retina work could eventually support vision-restoration therapies. Dragon stays docked until mid-November, then returns research samples for a Pacific splashdown — a reminder that SpaceX's routine cargo business keeps running underneath the AI spending headlines.

items.title: If smaller AI clouds collapse, SpaceX may be first in line to buy the pieces
items.summary:
A Motley Fool analysis argues SpaceX would be a prime beneficiary if debt-squeezed 'neocloud' AI computing firms fail, as Gartner predicts most will not stay independent by 2030 and billions in impairments loom. Because SpaceX standardized on Nvidia GPUs and Nvidia has backstop arrangements with many neoclouds, SpaceX could pick up distressed GPU clusters — and, more valuably, their power-grid access and site permits — at a discount.

It is a useful lens for Tuesday's SpaceX earnings and for the wider selloff: the firms with cash, power and permits survive a shakeout, while leveraged renters of compute face 15%-plus bond yields. Whether SpaceX is a buyer or just another heavy spender is the debate its results will feed.

items.title: Wichita driver released as police await toxicology and truck inspection after soccer tragedy
items.summary:
Wichita police released the 34-year-old driver on Sunday after interviewing more than 30 witnesses, pending toxicology results and a mechanical examination of her Chevrolet pickup, and no charges have been filed. Her truck barreled from a parking space onto a youth soccer field at the Stryker Sports Complex on Saturday, killing 6-year-old Adrian Cole and 35-year-old Nicholas Schafer, both of McPherson, and injuring 10 others ages 5 to 68, none with life-threatening injuries; two of her own children were in the truck and another was playing at the complex.

Police Chief Joe Sullivan said investigators know what happened but not yet why, and the toxicology and vehicle checks are now the whole case: they will determine whether this was a medical or mechanical failure, impairment, or something intentional. All events at the complex remain canceled, and police are asking anyone with video to come forward.

items.title: Bend mourns as investigators piece together how the school shooter got inside
items.summary:
Bend-La Pine Schools will stay closed through Tuesday, October 20, after Thursday's shooting at Silver Rail Elementary killed three children — ages 5, 8 and 11 — and 25-year-old teacher Megan Lambert, and left a 7-year-old girl and a 54-year-old teacher hospitalized. Police identified the shooter as Griffin J. John II, 16, a former student at the school, who forced his way in by firing through locked doors into the special-education classroom where he had once been a student; no motive has been announced.

The investigation now centers on access and the gun: the pump-action shotgun was purchased by his mother, according to a law-enforcement official, and the classroom remains a crime scene through at least October 20. Students return Wednesday on an early-release schedule, with Silver Rail itself closed until further notice.

items.title: A Bend father who followed the shooter into the school is hailed as a hero
items.summary:
New police detail from Bend describes three civilians who tried to stop Thursday's attack: a driver in a red pickup who confronted the shooter at the fence, was shot at repeatedly and called 911; a teacher who struggled with the gunman inside; and a father of two Silver Rail students, identified by his mother as lifelong Bend resident Kaylub Giamanco, who retrieved his legally carried gun from his car, followed the shooter inside and killed him. Governor Tina Kotek thanked the man who intervened, noting the heavy emotional burden he now carries.

Oregon's story this weekend is grief braided with that intervention — the attack lasted about three minutes, and officials credit the civilians with preventing further loss of life. Giamanco has asked for privacy, and how the community honors both the victims and the people who acted will shape the memorials planned as schools reopen this week.

items.title: 'No Kings: Vote Early' rallies shift from protest to getting ballots cast
items.summary:
The No Kings network held rallies across the country on Saturday billed this time as nonpartisan voter participation rather than pure protest, urging people to make a plan and vote early in the November 3 midterms. At the Lincoln Memorial a band played for a few hundred people in caps and coats holding 'VOTE EARLY' and 'HANDS OFF MY VOTE!' signs, and dozens of events ran across Maryland alone, with similar turnouts reported from Oklahoma City to Alexandria, Virginia.

Organizers say early voting is the best defense against interference, while President Trump continues to criticize mail-in voting — a method he uses himself. Polls suggest Democrats are poised to retake the House with the Senate too close to call, so the practical fight for the next two weeks is turnout mechanics: who banks their votes early and who waits for Election Day.

items.title: Norte Fire crews gain ground, but Santa Ana winds keep Southern California on edge
items.summary:
The Norte Fire, which ignited Friday near San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano in Orange County, burned 570 acres, destroyed or damaged six homes and forced evacuations affecting roughly 16,000 residents at its peak, with two firefighters hospitalized in stable condition. By Saturday evening containment had reached about 25% and most evacuation orders were lifted, though officials warned conditions remained volatile in gusty Santa Ana winds and 95-degree heat.

Norte is one of about ten wildfires burning across California this weekend, including the Bryson Fire in Malibu and the larger Henderson Fire in San Diego County, under red-flag warnings and a FEMA fire-assistance grant for Orange County. Whether the weekend's gains hold depends on the winds: another round of gusts could mean another round of evacuations.

items.title: Browns stun Ravens 13-10 on Szmyt's walk-off kick, grab a share of first place
items.summary:
The Browns beat Baltimore 13-10 at Huntington Bank Field on Sunday on Andre Szmyt's 37-yard field goal as time expired — redemption after he missed a 48-yarder wide left with 3:44 to play. Cleveland trailed 10-0 and had just 46 yards in the first half, but a Derrick Henry fumble set up Audric Estime's tying 2-yard touchdown, and Deshaun Watson's 33-yard strike to Jerry Jeudy (4 catches, 69 yards) set up the winner; the defense held Henry to 58 yards and Baltimore scoreless after the first quarter.

At 4-2, Cleveland owns a share of first in the AFC North this late in a season for the first time since 2014, plus the head-to-head tiebreaker over Baltimore. The concern is the offense, which needed another fourth-quarter rescue; the Browns visit Tennessee next Sunday needing a more complete performance, while Baltimore hosts Cincinnati.

items.title: Guardians trail early in pivotal ALCS Game 5 as Rays jump on Messick
items.summary:
Game 5 of the ALCS started at 5:08 p.m. Sunday at Progressive Field with the series tied 2-2, and Tampa Bay struck first: Parker Messick walked in a run with the bases loaded in a 31-pitch first inning, then Jonathan Aranda's RBI single made it 2-0 in the second as Messick's pitch count climbed past 57 with Tim Herrin warming. The Rays forced the swing game by winning Game 4 on Saturday 7-3, helped by Chase DeLauter's fielding error in right.

Whoever wins tonight flies to Florida up 3-2 and one win from the World Series, where Milwaukee waits; the loser faces elimination in Game 6 on Monday at Tropicana Field with no travel off-day after Friday's rainout. Cleveland's rested high-leverage bullpen — Hunter Gaddis, Erik Sabrowski and closer Cade Smith sat out the Game 4 blowout — is the Guardians' best path back into this one.

items.title: Ohio State turns to freshman Luke Fahey with Sayin out 'several weeks'
items.summary:
Ohio State held on to beat Indiana 19-15 on Saturday, but quarterback Julian Sayin left late in the fourth quarter after Mario Landino's sack pinned his throwing arm, returned to the sideline in a sling, and coach Ryan Day said he will miss several weeks. True freshman Luke Fahey finished the game — his first snaps in a top-five matchup after mop-up duty against Ball State and Kent State — and teammates like lineman Luke Montgomery publicly backed him: 'It's Fahey's time.'

The schedule does not wait: Ohio State goes to No. 19 USC next, then hosts Oregon and Northwestern before visiting Nebraska, all likely without a quarterback who had thrown for 2,007 yards and 19 touchdowns. How fast Fahey settles in — he went 0-for-2 with two punts in relief — will decide whether the Buckeyes' playoff path survives Sayin's absence.

items.title: Cleveland moves to extend its data center moratorium into early 2027
items.summary:
Cleveland City Council legislation would extend the city's pause on new data centers — set to expire October 20 — until January 29, 2027, after three town halls where residents raised power-grid, water-use and jobs concerns. Councilman Brian Kazy's Data Center Working Group studied laws elsewhere in Ohio, where about 125 local moratoriums were in place as of September and a state committee is still shaping House Bill 646.

Ohio has roughly 80 data centers operating and 189 planned, mostly around Columbus, and a developer just filed for a $1.6 billion, 150MW campus on East 55th Street that the extended moratorium could stall. The debate is the local version of the national AI build-out story: who pays for power and water, and whether the jobs justify it — expect the council vote and the state's bill to collide this winter.

items.title: Hopkins master plan would rebuild the airport around two concourses and 40 gates
items.summary:
Cleveland Hopkins unveiled its full Terminal Modernization Development Program master plan, replacing concourses A, B and C — 46 gates today — with two new concourses of about 40 gates, a new terminal headhouse, and an on-site rental-car facility on the old Concourse D site, ending the shuttle ride used since 1998. The expanded program is now estimated around $3 billion, with the ground transportation center due by 2029 and a new terminal possible by 2032.

Nothing about the full build is funded or final yet — the $301 million ground transportation center is the approved early step — but the plan sets Cleveland's pitch for the next decade of travel and for a possible hub return. Gate count actually shrinks, so the bet is on bigger, better facilities rather than more flights; watch the financing votes, not the renderings, for whether it becomes real.

items.title: Obama to rally in Cleveland Oct. 24 for Brown and Acton as Ohio races tighten
items.summary:
Former President Barack Obama will campaign in Cleveland on Saturday, October 24 with Senate candidate Sherrod Brown and gubernatorial nominee Dr. Amy Acton — his first Ohio visit since 2018. Brown is trying to unseat Sen. Jon Husted in the special election for JD Vance's old seat, and Acton faces Vivek Ramaswamy to succeed term-limited Gov. Mike DeWine; Obama praised Brown in a video for standing up to corporations, Wall Street and drug companies.

Ohio has drawn Trump and Vance for three rallies in 10 days, and now Obama is Democrats' first high-profile surrogate in the state — a sign both parties see the Senate race as close enough to decide control of the chamber. With gas and grocery prices the top voter complaint, the Cleveland rally kicks off the final ten days of a genuinely contested Ohio midterm.

baby.fact: Your baby already knows your voices. Babies start hearing around week 24, and newborns turn toward the voices they heard most before birth — all that talking to the bump counted.
